utterances.text: I had one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to each of those. But to set the stage, Hrasnica is south of the airport; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And where is Mount Igman in relation to Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: From Hrasnica, Mount Igman is the mountain going right up, straight up, into the hillside. The foot of Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. Would it be fair to say that Hrasnica is between Mount Igman and the airport?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Were there Bosnian army -- Bosnian Muslim troops in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And were there military targets in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not especially targets. I believe they were having their headquarters -- one company headquarter close to the front line, against Ilidza, and then battalion headquarters further east.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And during the time that you were in Hrasnica, you indicated that you had investigated incidents of sniping.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when you say you investigated incidents of sniping, what that means? You get to a sniping scene and a person has been shot. What do you do? Just walk us through the process, please.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, first we have to find out how this -- which way was this person facing when he was hit, and after that we have to investigate the body to see the incoming-outgoing wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: And from that we determine the direction it came, it's coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: During this time that you were in Hrasnica, would you say that the city of Sarajevo was under siege?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Would you say that Hrasnica was under siege?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Were you aware of where the confrontation lines were?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you investigate an incident of sniping in Hrasnica where you determined the source of fire to be anything other than a position in Bosnian Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Of the incidents of sniping that you investigated during your time in Hrasnica, how many times was it that a soldier or other member of the armed forces had been shot?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Sniping, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Turning now to shelling, and I'm speaking of mortars and artillery pieces. Air bomb will be later. How frequently did you investigate a shelling incident? How often?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Mr. Overgard, the pending question was how frequently did you investigate a shelling incident during your time as an UNMO in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, in the period of especially November and beginning of December 1994, it was nearly daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And I perhaps neglected to ask this question a few minutes ago. How frequently did you investigate an incident of sniping during your time in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Very often. It was also a lot of incidents of that. I can't say daily, but very often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Major, please, you said that you also investigated the bodies; you had to look at the bodies when there were sniping attacks. So I'd like to know whether you also work with forensic scientists? Do you work in isolation or do you work with the forensic scientist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We worked together with the civilian police of Hrasnica and inspected the bodies, but we did not turn them around or something. We just saw where is the incoming, where is the outgoing wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Major Overgard, just following up on His Honour's question, can you distinguish a gunshot wound of entrance from a gunshot wound of exit?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, of course. An incoming or ingoing wound is a -- more hole, but after the bullet -- when it goes out, it takes pieces with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: So a bigger hole and --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, a bigger hole, and you can clearly see where it comes out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: I asked you earlier how you went about investigating sniping incidents. I have the same question for shelling incidents. There is an explosion. A shell has fallen somewhere. You go to the scene. Just walk us through what happens next.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. You find the crater, and in the crater, normally the tail of the weapon is still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Why is that important?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Because when it is into solid ground, it has an angle, and from the angle you can determine where it was fired from. Not exactly but from which area, generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And what does -- the shape of the crater and the pattern with which things have been ejected from the crater, are those important things to consider as well?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. In the front of where it's coming from, it comes in at an angle, and in the front area we have a lot of more shrapnel and marks on the ground than in the back area, because when it has an angle coming in, it will spread that way out, and things coming out on the lower side will go straight down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And because the court reporter can't capture hand movements, I'll take the liberty of summarising in words what you were just demonstrating - and please correct me if I am wrong - that matter is ejected from the front of a crater. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We also use a compass then to get exactly which direction it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And from the angle, which you determine from the tail, and from the direction, which you determine from the ejection of debris pattern, can you determine where a particular mortar or artillery round was fired from?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, you can. Say it's a general area, not exactly, but you can be sure that it's in within a certain limited area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And I ask this question about sniping. I'll ask it again about mortaring and shelling. In your time at Hrasnica, did you ever investigate a shelling incident in which the source of fire was determined to be anything other than Bosnian Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And in the shelling incidents which you investigated during your time in Hrasnica, how many members of the armed forces lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There were not too many of them we saw, that's for sure. The investigations we did were normally for civilian -- when civilians had been targeted or hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention now to a type of weapon that is commonly referred to by the name "air bomb." If I use that word, do you know what I am referring to?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell the Court what you understand by the term "air bomb"?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: A bomb of the old type is something dropped over an area from an aeroplane, and that is an air bomb, just coming down somewhere in that area and dropping it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Were air bombs used in -- was there an incident of an air bomb being used in Hrasnica during your time there?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: What was the date of that incident?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: 7th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Was that bomb dropped from an aeroplane?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No. That's a -- I've never seen before or after that it comes -- fired from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: How was it done? Were you able to determine from your investigation how it came about that this bomb could be moved from the place of origin to the place of impact without using an aeroplane?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. It was tied up with six rockets, and the rockets were the engine for the bomb. It was then fired from a truck on the Ilidza side of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And when you say it was fired from a truck on the Ilidza side, two questions: First of all, was Ilidza under the control of the Bosnian Muslims or the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The Serbs, the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. And how did you come about the information that you've just told us about where this bomb was fired from?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It is -- the people on Mount Igman had witnessed this one, the direction it came from. That was from witness statements. And when it had landed, all the windows in that direction were broken for a couple hundred metres, for 300 metres. And that was not on the other side, on the eastern side of the crater there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And what conclusion were you able to draw from the fact that the windows were broken primarily on the eastern side of the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That the witness told us what happened and that was right, that it came --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: In other words, your investigation corroborated what the witness on Mount Igman had told you.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: What kind of an area had this bomb come down in?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Civilian houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Had anyone lost their life?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- did you go to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: When we arrived, we found the house totally demolished. There was nothing, not a brick standing nearly. One wall. But the side where the bomb hit was totally torn down to small bits and pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you see any human bodies in this rubble?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I saw one or two legs coming out some pile of stones. They were not moving. But as I discovered that, the local commander came and called upon us and said that we should not be there first to investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. And this was the -- when you say local commander, this was the commander of the Bosnian Muslim troops in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, 4th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And did you leave, as he had told you to do?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: How long were you gone from the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We went back to our accommodation, and when we came there, he had posted three soldiers there that would keep us inside our accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: How long were you inside your accommodation?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Until late that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: The next day did you return to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We tried to go up in the morning but then the soldiers were back again so we had to negotiate our movement, our freedom of movement again. Then around midday we were allowed to go back to the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And is that when you actually conducted the investigation that you've been describing for the last few minutes?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: As an air force officer, you, I take it, are familiar with bombs dropped from aeroplanes.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: This contraption that you saw on the 7th of April, 1995, what sort of guidance system did it have?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was no guidance. It was launched in another direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: What determined --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just and minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Witness. And I apologise, counsel. We perhaps should settle the ways in which we do this. But you were speaking just a while ago, Mr. Witness, about the fact that you were held back in your accommodation for some hours, I understand, by three soldiers. What was the purpose of restricting your access to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never got a good answer on that. It was the commander of the brigade in that area that wanted us inside. I think he wanted to have people from Sarajevo into the area first, and so we did not disturb their investigation, I think, expert -- bomb experts and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Following up on His Honour's question, Major, when you're doing an investigation, is it important that people not go into a scene and disturb things before an investigation is done?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, for sure. Then you can -- they can turn bits and pieces. So it seems for us that it comes from another direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Yes. And when you say that people were coming from Sarajevo, did you understand these people from Sarajevo to be experts in ballistics and explosives?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, we talked with them later on, and then they showed us everything, all the bits and pieces, and -- they had collected everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Do you understand, or is it your opinion, that it was important that the scene be undisturbed until these experts arrived --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: -- from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: So we did the investigation of that one to get -- more or less altogether. We returned to that one later that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. And had this sort of thing happened in earlier investigations where you were restricted from a scene by Bosnian Muslim troops?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: This was a one-time event?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Again, as an air force officer, have you had training during your 20-plus years in the Norwegian Air Force in what sorts of weapons are appropriate for what sorts of battlefield situations?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Can you think of a battlefield situation in which this sort of air bomb with rocket engines strapped on is an appropriate weapon?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And is that because it cannot be guided?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It cannot be guided or -- and you will never know where it will explode, and when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Have you, before coming to court today, looked at photographs of this incident on the 7th of April in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. And in your view, are those photographs accurate depictions of what happened that day and what you saw when you arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, may I ask that ter number 2719 be called up and displayed. This is a series of photographs, Your Honour, and we have indicated with our exhibit submission the ERN numbers of the specific photographs that we wish to display, and I would ask that the witness, having indicated that these are true and accurate photographs, that these be admitted as they are displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I believe the first photograph is ERN 0094-5320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you going to ask the witness to say what this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, I don't know -- could I have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm just checking to see if better quality photographs are available --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sorry. If I could just have a moment or two. It may take a moment or two to check, but we'll try and get some better photographs, or if it's not possible, I guess we'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, may I ask, how is the showing of these photographs essential to your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It illustrates the destructive power of the weapon used, Your Honour. They are pictures of utterly demolished brick houses. And in light of the regrettable difficulty we're having in getting good quality photographs, I will limit myself to showing -- I do have better quality ones, but I would ask leave to put in a smaller number of photographs and use the ELMO to display them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That would be a better course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Major, I'm not going to ask you detailed questions about these photographs. I believe they speak for themselves. I'm simply going to ask you to verify that this is an accurate depiction of what you saw at that scene in Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. This was the house we arrived at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was that one house or two houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a house and the -- a kind of barn or something beside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: The same question as this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, could we perhaps have and better photograph? Does everybody have the same picture on his on her screen? Because on my screen I can't see anything at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you must go to the ELMO now. This is now on the ELMO. Have you pressed the ELMO button?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we have the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Major, at this point may I ask, was there damage to other houses as well even if they were not destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, they were. The roofs, there were holes in them after the blast, and windows were gone as well. We talked about that also.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: This appears to be a close-up of the one before. And then I believe the last photograph. Thank you. That concludes the review of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll ask that these photographs which were on the -- poorer-quality copies which were on the exhibit list be marked and put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Is counsel asking for that group of photographs to be admitted as one exhibit or individual exhibit numbers to be given to each photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir, they could be admitted as a single exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P84.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Major, did you ever see these air bombs before firing on the Bosnian Muslim side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you ever see launchers for such devices on the Bosnian Muslim side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [No audible answer].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And lastly was there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was the answer to that question? Did you ever see launchers for such devices on the Bosnian Muslim side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please answer orally, not just by nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: On the map that was in evidence a little while ago, Major, there was a green dot with the number 6 beside it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you examine that before coming to court?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Does that green dot accurately indicate the location at which this occurred?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And how far away is the impact of this air bomb from the two military headquarters that you mentioned earlier that were in Hrasnica, the company headquarters and the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Very far. It was more close to our accommodation, team location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And I guess the same question, then: How far from your accommodation were these headquarters? Would it be measured in kilometres, in metres, in what unit?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: A hundred metres, I can say. To the company headquarters, it's more like a kilometre or so, and 800 or 900 metres from our -- from our accommodation to the battalion headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: All right. Was there -- I'm going to ask about another incident now. Was there a time, to take a sniping incident as an example, of a 17-year-old girl being shot and killed by a sniper in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you see this girl while she was still alive?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Whereabouts was she when you saw her still alive?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: She was walking in the area called Solakovici, from where they started to dig a tunnel under the airport into Sarajevo, and she was working towards Solakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And were you driving when you saw her?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. We had passed her on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: As she was walking from Solakovici to Hrasnica, which side of her, her right or her left, would be towards the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It would be her back side or left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Back left?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Later on did you investigate a sniping incident involving this girl?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. I was called upon by the civilian policeman to join him to inspect a victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And how long after you had seen her walking were you called to investigate this incident?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: One hour, maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you view her body?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And was there a gunshot wound of entrance on her body?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was a 12.7 or something in that -- 14.6, I think they used, millimetre. It was a big hole and a big outgoing. So it was bigger than the 7.62 weapon that had been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And whereabouts had the bullet entered her?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: In her upper body, from back on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Back left. Did you or your colleagues at Sierra Sierra 1 ever file protests with Bosnian Serb military commanders regarding sniping or shelling or air bombing?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No. The teams are not to do this job. It is for the UNMO headquarters that was located inside Sarajevo in the PTT building. They sent out this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just ask, what was the size of the entrance wound and the exit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- let's say the hole and the blue area around there was more than 5 centimetres, but I can't remember the exact. The policeman did the measurement. I was on that investigation also alone, because no other can follow me. Normally we're always two UNMOs together when we are doing investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That was the entrance, around 5 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the exit was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a big hole in her. I can say, well, 10, 20 centimetres out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what is the diameter of a 12.7 bullet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is -- okay. I can say 3, 3 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Two last things, Major, and then I'll be finished. Were you aware of a road that ran over Mount Igman and down into Hrasnica and on into Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. It is referred as the Blue Road, or we call it the convoy road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: What was that road used for during your time in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was all supplies to Sarajevo, Hrasnica and Sarajevo, came that way, with food, with everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did civilians try and use that road?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you ever observe those civilians being fired upon?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: From your position in Hrasnica, could you tell that these were civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And were you able to conclude which side it was that was firing upon these civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Firing to the convoy road came from Ilidza area on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And when you say that you were able to tell they were civilians, how far away were these civilians from you when you were able to tell those are civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: From our accommodation of our team, our team location, we were situated just at the foot of Igman, so less than a kilometre, and we also observed this and reported a lot of times from the OP we had in the Sierra Whisky area, Whisky 1 area, Blue 3 team area, at the end of airfield on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Did you have any trouble telling these people were civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Was there a bridge in the Butmir area that was used by civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. It was used by civilians, by us, by everyone going into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Were you ever able to observe civilians using the Butmir bridge?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Again, from where you were, did you have any difficulty at all in telling that these were civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what side it was that was firing upon these civilians?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: Which side was it?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It came from the Serb side, from the Ilidza side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHTERY
utterances.text: And then lastly, sir, during your time in Hrasnica, limiting it to you, your time in Hrasnica, investigations you conducted, how many dead civilians did you see as a result of sniping and shelling?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Personally I have not summarised it, but it has to be 30 -- between 30 and 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No further questions on direct examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have to inform you that it has been brought to our attention that there is a severe storm affecting the area, and in fact we have been advised that the staff of the Tribunal has been authorised to leave in light of the serious weather conditions. The Tribunal staff are permitted to leave the Tribunal so as to reach their home as soon as practically possible. However, the Ministry of the Interior has issued an advice recommending that people consider staying indoors. I have just been informed that a message is being broadcast over the loudspeaker system indicating what I have just told you. In light of this, what I propose to do is to take a break of 20 minutes, and when we resume, I'll tell you what the Chamber's decision is as to whether we'll continue or not. So we will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I just want to make the announcement on the microphone so everyone can hear: We are standing down and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of January, 2007, at 9.30 a.m.
